subject: Recap & data ask: deployment-mode criteria and pilot options
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.inference.com>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@brightcart.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2028-06-20T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Recap & data ask: deployment-mode criteria and pilot options

Hi Alex —

Great to speak earlier. Quick recap of what I heard and the asks we discussed so we can align internal folks (Ben + Marissa) and propose the right pilot: 

Summary of BrightCart requirements from call:
- Model: LlamaX-13B (quantized variant OK)
- Typical traffic: steady baseline with sharp retail peaks (you mentioned Black Friday–like bursts)
- Peak concurrent QPS observed today: ~3.2k (peak window), average ~600–800 QPS
- Latency targets: P50 <100ms, P99 target ~<250ms (you noted current infra shows P99 ~280ms during peaks)
- Context lengths: up to ~4k tokens for a subset of requests (multi-turn chat style)
- Batch tolerance: low — many requests are sync and user-facing (cannot accept long batching delays)
- Data/security note: prefer Hosted for speed of launch but expect VPC/on-prem requirement for production procurement later

Immediate asks / next steps from our side:
1) Could you share an anonymized 48–72h traffic sample (timestamps, request sizes, qps time series, and a few example payloads)? this helps us select kernels, sizing, and caching configuration.
2) Please confirm which flows require strict P99 SLAs vs those that can tolerate degraded tails.
3) We’ll propose two pilot paths after we see the sample:
   - Hosted pilot (fastest): Hosted API with reserved burst nodes + KV/prefix caching and explicit cold-start mitigations. 30–60 day pilot to validate tail latency at scale.
   - Dedicated pilot (controls): Dedicated GPU pool (reserved) sized for your peak; more predictable tail but longer provisioning.
   - Long-term: Private VPC/on-prem evaluation for production (compliance/procurement dependent).

I attached a short pilot-options overview (pilot-options-overview.pdf) — it maps tradeoffs and typical timelines. Ben and Marissa are looped for sizing and infra details.

If you can send the traffic sample and Sam (your infra lead) is available for a 60m technical deep dive this week, we can return a concrete pilot proposal by EOW.

Thanks —
Jordan
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.inference.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

--
Attachment: pilot-options-overview.pdf (application/pdf, 128KB)
From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@brightcart.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Sam Patel <sam.patel@brightcart.com>
Date: 2028-06-20T17:38:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap & data ask: deployment-mode criteria and pilot options

Thanks Jordan — good recap. A few clarifications and I attached a first pass of a traffic bundle.

Answers to your asks:
- We attached a 48-hour qps/time CSV (brightcart_prod_48h_qps.csv) plus a small payload sample set (brightcart_payload_samples.json). The 48h sample includes a 3.2k QPS spike that lasted ~12 minutes (11:21–11:33am PT).
- P50 numbers from our current service are ~85ms for the common short requests; P99 drifts to ~275–320ms under peak load for the long-context flows.
- Percent of requests with long contexts (~>2k tokens): ~8% of traffic but those generate disproportionate CPU/GPU time.
- Most requests are synchronous and user-facing; we can tolerate small batching (20–50ms) for non-critical routes but cannot batch checkout-related flows.
- Compliance: for now SOC2 evidence is fine, but procurement has flagged a VPC option as probable requirement for production contract (8–12 week lead time).
- Procurement window: target decision in ~6–10 weeks depending on procurement cycle.

Sam is available for a technical deep dive Friday 6/22 at 10:00 PT — does that work for you and Ben/Marissa?

We are open to starting with Hosted pilot if the tail mitigations look promising, but we want clear visibility on P99 at expected peaks before committing.

Alex Morgan
Head of Platform Engineering | BrightCart
alex.morgan@brightcart.com | +1 (650) 555-3410

Attachments: brightcart_prod_48h_qps.csv (text/csv, 42KB); brightcart_payload_samples.json (application/json, 18KB)
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.inference.com>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@brightcart.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>, Sam Patel <sam.patel@brightcart.com>
Date: 2028-06-20T18:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap & data ask: deployment-mode criteria and pilot options

Alex — appreciate the fast turnaround and the files. Downloaded and started a quick pass. A couple clarifying Qs so we size the pilot correctly before Friday: 

1) Are requests routed through an edge cache/ingress (e.g., CDN) such that some percentage are terminated before hitting the model? if so, what percentage?
2) For the long-context payloads, what is the typical token distribution (e.g., 2k–3k vs 3k–4k)? any examples in the payload sample are helpful.
3) Do you have a small set of business-critical routes that must never exceed the P99 target (please name them)?

Proposed pilot options (high level) — we’ll come with a concrete sizing doc on Friday: 
- Option A — Hosted pilot (fastest start): start on Hosted API with reserved burst nodes, enable prefix/KV caching for repeated contexts, explicit cold-start pre-warming for heavy models. Expected turnaround: 1–2 weeks to get scale test harness running + 2–4 weeks of load testing.
- Option B — Dedicated pilot: we provision a dedicated pool sized for your 3.2k peak and validate tails across traffic sample. Longer lead time (provisioning + tuning), but usually better tail predictability.
- Option C — Private VPC path: mostly for procurement/long-term. We can spin that up in parallel to contract negotiations if needed.

Ben/Marissa — can you join Friday 10:00 PT? Ben, can you bring rough GPU counts for a dedicated pool for an initial 3.2k peak using LlamaX-13B quantized assumptions? Marissa — can you prepare a one-page tail-mitigation runbook (pre-warm, cache rules, streaming config) so we can show BrightCart what hosted mitigations look like?

If Friday at 10:00 PT works, I’ll send a calendar invite and a short agenda (traffic walk, architecture implications, pilot timeline).

Jordan

Jordan/Ben/Marissa —

Friday 10:00 PT works for us. Sam will join and bring the infra diagrams. A couple quick confirmations before the call:

- We confirmed a subset of critical routes: /checkout/price, /checkout/validate, /search/quick (these three must stay within P99 SLA).
- Edge termination: roughly 15% of requests are cached at the CDN level; the attached 48h data is post-edge (so it reflects actual requests hitting your runtime).
- Long-context distribution: in the sample, ~70% of long-context hits are in the 2k–3k token range; ~30% are 3k–4k.
- We attach the two files again here in case someone missed them.

We’re comfortable starting an exploratory Hosted pilot provided Redwood can demonstrate P99 <300ms at predicted peaks with the pilot harness. If hosted cannot meet the tail after obvious mitigations, we expect to pivot to Dedicated for prod. Procurement timeline still ~8 weeks for contract/VPC.

See you Friday — I’ll send a calendar invite now.

Alex

Attachments: brightcart_prod_48h_qps.csv; brightcart_payload_samples.json
